turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey, you got a sec? I need to run something by you about the DNS cutover.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Sure, what's up? I thought we were doing that next week.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, well, I got impatient. I pointed the DNS at the new cluster this morning before it was fully ready.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Oh no. Please tell me you didn't send live traffic to it.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: I did. And guess what? It couldn't serve it. I saw the error rates spike in the dashboard and flipped it back within five minutes.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: That's a classic. You're lucky it wasn't worse. So what's the plan now?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: I'm going to wait for the cluster health check to pass before I even think about switching DNS again. I learned my lesson.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Good. Let me know when you're ready to retry. I can help you watch the metrics.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Alright, the health check finally went green. I'm about to switch DNS now.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Nice. You waited this time, right?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yep, waited for the full health check to pass. No shortcuts this time.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Okay, I'm watching the traffic graphs. Go ahead.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Done. Traffic moved over without a hitch. Latency looks stable, no errors.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Beautiful. See? Patience pays off. Now we can finally retire the old cluster.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, I'll start the decommission process tomorrow. Thanks for keeping an eye on things.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Hey, I was digging through the query logs from the new cluster and I found something concerning.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: What do you mean? I thought everything was clean after the cutover.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Well, I noticed you logged sensitive data to the query log. Like, full customer payloads with PII.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Wait, what? I didn't think I had verbose logging enabled. That's bad.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: It's worse than bad. Customer data leaked into the logs. I'm seeing email addresses and account numbers in there.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Oh no. I must have left the debug flag on from the testing phase. I need to purge those logs immediately.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: You need to do more than purge. We have to notify security and probably the affected customers. This is a data breach.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: You're right. I'll escalate this right now. I'm sorry, Kim. I really screwed up.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: We'll get through it. But let's fix the logging config first, then deal with the fallout.
